newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market doubts German repo cut talk.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market doubts German repo cut talk.

text.p: Dutch money market dealers doubted German speculation on Wednesday that the Bundesbank may cut its repo rate tomorrow during its fortnightly meeting.
Earlier today rumours from Germany that the repo rate might be trimmed by 20 basis points on Thursday boosted bunds.
"I'm a disbeliever of the rumours," said one dealer, adding in his view the shave would be 10 basis points at the most, although it was more likely that rates would be left unchanged.
Another dealer was also questioning the rumour, adding it was only wishful thinking. "The Bundesbank is probably waiting for the latest M3 figure first," he said
The German September M3 money growth figure is not due until October 18 at the earliest, according to the official diary.
Analysts have not given a forecast yet for the latest M3 figure. In August the German M3 growth was 8.7 percent versus 8.6 percent in the previous month.
The German central bank said in August its target for M3 growth was between four and seven percent.
"In the meantime other data, like Tuesday's German unemployment, add to the idea that the repo could be trimmed," said one dealer.
The Dutch equavalent, the special advances rate, is fixed at 2.50 percent and the Dutch central bank will set a new pact on Monday.
"If Germany, but this is not likely, trims the repo rate by 20 basis points, the Dutch advances could be cut by 10 basis points," said one dealer.
Dealers said trade was about moderate with prices lingering near previous levels.
Call money was trading at 2.68-2.75 percent bid. Three-month deposits climbed up three basis points to 2.78 percent bid.
